fields.description:
## Context / Problem
A Jira update currently crosses `dispatch_one._update_one_scalar_update`, generic `dispatch_apply_phases._call_with_retry`, Cloud ACLI retry, or Jira DC SDK and `_with_connection_retry` loops. A timeout can multiply calls or leave an accepted write ambiguous. Jira updates expose no Rebar-controlled idempotency key, so recovery needs desired-state observation instead of blind replay.

## Outcome
Prove the provider-neutral contract by setting an issue summary to an exact value. Cloud follows `dispatch_one._update_one_scalar_update -> AcliClient.update_issue(key, summary=...)`; DC terminates at `_IssuesMixin.update_issue(key, summary=...)`. Both execute under one logical-operation budget. This story establishes ADR 0100; RP-03 S3 owns production cutover and terminal-outcome consumption, and RP-03 S5 finalizes the ADR after all families migrate.

## Approach
1. Define operation/outcome values with stable logical id, desired postcondition, attempt count, disposition, failure scope, replay safety, provider delay, `retry_not_before`, plus bounded redacted diagnostics.
2. A physical invocation is one executor call to an adapter write or observation, not each required request inside it. Count raw provider requests separately. The shared owner permits three physical invocations and 15 seconds cumulative sleep across initial write, observation, plus safe replan. Use `2**(attempt+1) + U[0,1)` jitter: [2s,3s) then [4s,5s). Reuse `_errors.parse_retry_after`; provider delay is a lower bound.
3. Add a constructor-injected internal route selector at the dispatch seam. It defaults to legacy in S1, unit and credential-free integration tests explicitly select the executor, and it is not a user config key or environment variable. Only an exact `{"summary"}` field set is eligible. Mixed `{"summary","description"}` stays one unsplit legacy call. There is no dual-send. S3 owns venue-gated validation and the default-on production cutover.
4. Cloud writes launch one ACLI process; cleanup uses POSIX group reap or non-POSIX child kill/bounded wait. No replay occurs below the budget. Decode only sanitized exit/stdout/stderr; unknown shapes fail loud. Recovery uses `AcliClient.get_issue_by_rest` against primary-store `GET /rest/api/3/issue/{key}`, never indexed ACLI JQL. Add a per-call retry-policy argument to `acli_rest._rest_urlopen_with_retry`; only the summary recovery observation supplies single-attempt/no-sleep. Every existing access-check and REST caller retains the current three-attempt, 2s/5s behavior. A poison test proves that the selected observation performs exactly one raw request and no inner sleep.
5. Construct a dedicated DC executor client with `jira.JIRA(..., max_retries=0)` and a fail-fast session guard. Do not change the legacy DC client or its current SDK retry policy in S1. The selected executor invokes each pre-read/write/read-back through `_with_connection_retry` under an injected single-attempt/no-sleep policy; every legacy caller retains the current wrapper policy until its later migration.
6. One selected DC summary-write invocation has fixed raw requests GET issue -> PUT fields -> GET read-back, with no SDK/wrapper repeats. Failure ends that invocation. Successful read-back is authoritative; after ambiguous PUT, a separate GET observation consumes the next physical invocation. Tests assert top-level attempts and raw order.
7. After ambiguous timeout, desired summary observed means recovered success. A conclusive old value may replay inside remaining budget. Failed, rate-limited, or inconclusive observation returns non-replaying `commit_unknown` with deferral metadata; no fallthrough write.
8. Worked example: DC invocation 1 issues GET then ambiguous PUT; observation 2 issues one GET that times out. Return `commit_unknown` after two invocations, three GET/PUT requests total, including one PUT. If observation 2 returns the old summary, invocation 3 may run GET/PUT/GET; no fourth invocation. A poison sleeper proves `_with_connection_retry` never delays or replays on this route.
9. Credential, TLS, permission, invalid-request, plus other permanent failures do not retry. Eligible network failures, 429, plus retryable 5xx use the shared schedule. An authoritative delay that cannot fit returns `retry_not_before` without early sleep or fictional attempt.
10. Preserve the current `update_one` / `apply_handlers.handle_update` boundary while the S1 selector is test-only. `dispatch_one` maps success and recovered success to the existing result dict and fills `_fields_synced` for summary only after conclusive success; `_comment_errors` and `_subop` retain their current shapes. `commit_unknown` and `retry_not_before` map to an internal tagged result consumed by `handle_update`, which records a bounded per-mutation error/disposition, leaves `_fields_synced` empty, advances neither baseline nor set-field provenance, and persists no deferral record in S1. The rest of the batch can continue. S3 is the authoritative consumer: it maps these dispositions into pass/fuse control and durable deferral, then retires this temporary compatibility bridge at production cutover.
11. Emit one bounded redacted operation-completion log for `commit_unknown`, `retry_not_before`, exhaustion, plus child cleanup failure. Tests pin fields, level, redaction, and size.
12. Establish ADR 0100 with the contract, retry owner, Jira idempotency limitation, observe-before-replay rationale, budget, lifecycle ownership, deltas, plus rollback. Relate ADR 0084/0087 and desired-state ADRs 0004/0026/0029: observation reuses existing convergence; the new decision is one budget across dispatch, CLI, SDK, and adapter loops. The 15-second cumulative budget supersedes ADR 0084 60-second per-sleep cap only for selected routes; longer delays become `retry_not_before`.

## Scope
- `operation_outcome.py`, `retry_budget.py`: contract and sole budget.
- `dispatch_one.py`, `dispatch_apply_phases.py`: internal legacy-default selector, route, outcome compatibility bridge, and generic-wrapper bypass.
- `apply_handlers.py`: consume the temporary tagged terminal outcomes without false success, baseline advance, or provenance write.
- Cloud `acli.py`, `acli_subprocess.py`, `acli_rest.py`, and backend: one-process execution, per-call single-attempt observation policy, decoding, cleanup, typed surface; preserve unrelated REST retry defaults.
- DC `transport.py`, `retry.py`, `_issues.py`, and backend: dedicated no-SDK-retry executor client, per-call one-attempt wrapper policy, fixed request shape; preserve legacy client behavior.
- ADR 0100, budget/outcome and handler tests, historical ACLI fixtures, reaping regressions, and DC request tests.

## Testing
- Fake-clock tables assert attempts, requests, sleep, deadlines, provider lower bounds, plus `retry_not_before` with no real sleep.
- Stateful Cloud/DC fakes cover success, disconnect, ambiguity, inconclusive observation, recovery, 429/503, malformed delay, TLS/auth/permanent 4xx, plus request order.
- Poison tests fail on generic retry, summary-observation inner retry/sleep, DC wrapper replay/sleep, SDK retry, or an extra ACLI process. Neighbor tests prove existing Cloud REST and legacy DC retry behavior is unchanged.
- Compatibility tests exercise `handle_update`: confirmed outcomes alone fill `_fields_synced`; terminal outcomes record an error/disposition but cannot advance baseline or provenance.
- Historical ACLI triples pin decoding; unknown shapes fail loud. Real child-process tests prove reaping.
- Output tests pin logs, redaction, bounded diagnostics, plus fast-fail behavior. Required tests are local and credential-free; S3 owns venue-gated cutover evidence and S5 owns live confirmation before contract removal.

## Compatibility / Rollback
S1 leaves production on the legacy route through an internal constructor default, so rollback is selecting legacy before a call; there is no new config or environment surface and no dual-send. S3 may switch the internal default only after its venue-gated evidence passes. Rollback preserves successful effects, then re-observes ambiguity. Intentional selected-route deltas are the shared three-invocation/15-second budget, long-delay deferral, fail-loud unknown ACLI shapes, plus non-replaying inconclusive recovery. Unselected Cloud REST and DC callers retain current retry behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Both summary routes produce the same provider-neutral outcome schema; deterministic tests assert every field.
- [ ] Repeated physical invocations preserve one logical id; a unit test asserts identity stability.
- [ ] Top-level counters prove no selected postcondition exceeds three invocations or 15 seconds cumulative sleep.
- [ ] Raw counters prove each selected DC write invocation follows GET/PUT/GET without hidden repeats.
- [ ] Cloud ambiguity uses one primary-store REST GET under a per-call single-attempt/no-sleep policy; neighbor tests prove all unrelated REST callers retain three attempts and 2s/5s backoff.
- [ ] When the selector enables the executor, exact `{"summary"}` bypasses `_call_with_retry`; a poison test proves it.
- [ ] The selector is constructor-injected, defaults to legacy, and adds no config or environment key; tests explicitly enable it.
- [ ] Mixed fields stay one legacy call; a table test proves no split.
- [ ] Success and recovered success map to the existing result, `_fields_synced`, `_comment_errors`, and `_subop` shapes.
- [ ] `commit_unknown` and `retry_not_before` become bounded per-mutation errors with no baseline/provenance advance and no S1 deferral persistence; handler tests prove each negative.
- [ ] The S1 contract and ADR identify S3 as the sole cutover, fuse-consumer, deferral-persistence, and compatibility-bridge retirement owner.
- [ ] The dedicated DC executor client passes `max_retries=0` and enforces the session guard; neighbor tests prove the legacy client policy is unchanged.
- [ ] Selected DC calls use single-attempt/no-sleep `_with_connection_retry`; poison and neighbor tests reject selected-route replay while preserving legacy behavior.
- [ ] Fallback sleeps stay in [2s,3s), then [4s,5s); fake-clock tests pin bounds.
- [ ] Over-budget provider delay returns `retry_not_before` without sleeping.
- [ ] Permanent failures perform one invocation; transient failures follow the injected schedule.
- [ ] Satisfied post-timeout observation returns recovered success without a second write.
- [ ] Conclusively unsatisfied observation permits only remaining-budget replay.
- [ ] Failed or inconclusive observation returns non-replaying `commit_unknown`; the example asserts two invocations, three raw requests, one PUT.
- [ ] ACLI cleanup tests pass for POSIX groups and non-POSIX direct children.
- [ ] Historical ACLI triples decode as expected; an unknown triple returns unclassified without retry.
- [ ] Completion logs expose deferred/exhausted outcomes without secret or unbounded content.
- [ ] ADR 0100 records the contract, lifecycle ownership, compatibility deltas, and prior-art relationships; index checks pass.
